subject: botany
question_text: Who are herbalists? What are the books written by them?

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Who herbalists were
lines: Herbalists were the people who identified
and described medicinal plants during the
steps.why: The definition has three parts and all three are marked: what they did (identified and described), which plants (medicinal), and when (16th and 17th centuries).
common_mistakes: Leaving out 'medicinal' — herbalists worked on medicinal plants, not all plants.
Leaving out the centuries — the time period is part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Herbalists in three parts: did what (identified and described), which plants (medicinal), when (16th-17th centuries).
steps.margin_note: One sentence with all three parts: did what, which plants, when.

steps.label: Their books

lines.text: The books written by herbalists are called Herbals.

lines: Herbals record the names, descriptions and
steps.why: The second half asks only for the name of the books; 'Herbals' is the one word the examiner looks for.
common_mistakes: Writing 'herbaria' — a herbarium is a store of pressed plant specimens, not a book.
Writing 'herbalists' again for the books — the people are herbalists, the books are Herbals.
steps.memory_tip: Drop the -ist: the herbalist (person) wrote the Herbal (book).
steps.margin_note: The boxed word Herbals is the whole second mark.

insider_note: Herbals and herbarium look alike and examiners watch for the swap — only Herbals is the book.
